title: Visible allowance: a softer landing at the usage limit
intro: Free users find the photo and image tools. What makes them leave is a limit they couldn’t see, arriving in the middle of a task. In 147 negative App Store reviews, 54 were about usage limits and only 1 was about finding a feature.

today.title: No count where you choose
today.text: The tools sheet doesn’t say how many uses are left. Since Aug 2026 the count exists, but only in Settings › Usage.

today.title: The wall comes after sending
today.text: The limit appears only once the request is sent. The only way out is to upgrade, so the offer reads as a punishment.

proposal.title: The count sits on the chip
proposal.text: “Photos · 3 left today” appears where the decision is made, not hidden in settings.

proposal.title: A warning before the last use
proposal.text: One line above the composer, no pop-up. The chip turns amber.

proposal.title: Three equal ways forward
proposal.text: Save it for later, do it in text, or upgrade. The message and photo are kept, so nothing is lost.

proposal.title: One place to check
proposal.text: Text is unlimited, tools show “0 of 3 left”, the reset time is clear, and failed results don’t count.

lessons: Put the meter where the decision happens, not in a settings page.
Warn before the limit, not after. A surprise at the moment of highest intent is what people remember.
Give more than one way out. Upgrading works better as one choice among several than as the only exit.
test: Does seeing the meter make people ration their use? If 3 of 5 testers hold back because they can see the count, the idea needs rethinking.
note: Independent study by Mitul Vaghasiya, not affiliated with ChatGPT. Every screen below is my re-creation in ChatGPT’s visual style, based on its App Store screenshots (10 Oct 2026) and the public images listed in references/. They are not screenshots of the real app.

compare.title: Hitting the photo limit: before and after
compare.question: A free user is editing photos and runs out of uses. The same tasks, two designs.

before.try: Tap ＋ → Photos, pick any photo and send. Do it four times.
before.notice: Nothing shows how many uses are left. The fourth send hits a wall with one way out: upgrade.

after.try: Do the same: ＋ → Photos, pick a photo, send, four times.
after.notice: The chip counts down, a warning comes before the last use, and at the limit you get three choices. Your photo is kept.
